output.reason: Reported itchy blistery rash confined to both forearms 2+ days after direct poison ivy exposure, with fever and breathing trouble denied; apparent local spread is consistent with delayed sensitization rather than infection or systemic illness. No decision-critical uncertainty currently requires clinician assessment, prescribing or testing, so guidance plus a symptom-specific safety net is sufficient.
output.patientMessage: You can manage this at home for now with over-the-counter itch relief; a pharmacist can advise on options. A poison ivy rash often looks like it is spreading as lower-exposure skin reacts, which fits what you describe. If the rash becomes painful rather than itchy, spreads well beyond your forearms, involves your face, eyes or genitals, weeps pus, or you develop fever, arrange a same-day in-person visit; if you cannot get one, go to urgent care. If you develop trouble breathing or throat tightness, call 911.
differential: Allergic contact dermatitis from urushiol (poison ivy), consistent with exposure history and vesicular forearm rash
Secondary bacterial infection or cellulitis — pain, warmth or fever would suggest this; not reported either way apart from denied fever
More extensive/severe contact dermatitis that could warrant prescription treatment; total body surface involvement beyond forearms not reported
